Playbook.name: Windows — Inhibit System Recovery (Ransomware Precursor) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A command to delete backups/shadow copies ran - vssadmin/wmic shadowcopy delete, bcdedit recovery disable, or wbadmin delete. This is the step ransomware takes just before encryption. Triage question: is this a ransomware precursor, or a legitimate admin/backup maintenance action?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Deleting shadow copies removes the ability to recover from encryption - almost always immediately precedes ransomware detonation.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Recovery inhibition
Signal.Details: vssadmin/wmic shadowcopy delete, bcdedit recoveryenabled no, wbadmin delete.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the recovery-inhibition command is a ransomware precursor or sanctioned maintenance.

Step.name: Confirm the recovery-inhibition command
Step.Purpose: The exact command distinguishes shadow-copy deletion (ransomware tell) from routine bcdedit.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE (cl LIKE "*vssadmin*" AND cl LIKE "*delete*shadow*") OR (cl LIKE "*wmic*" AND cl LIKE "*shadowcopy*delete*") OR (cl LIKE "*bcdedit*" AND cl LIKE "*recoveryenabled*no*") OR (cl LIKE "*wbadmin*" AND cl LIKE "*delete*") OR cl LIKE "*wbadmin delete catalog*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, user.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: vssadmin delete shadows /all is the classic ransomware precursor. Note the account - SYSTEM/normal-user context by a non-backup process is malicious. A backup admin rotating catalogs under a window is benign.

Step.name: Signs of mass file changes on the host (encryption underway)
Step.Purpose: Shadow deletion followed by mass file writes is active ransomware - this is time-critical.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "11" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 30 minutes | STATS files = COUNT(*), procs = VALUES(process.name), exts = VALUES(file.extension) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A spike of file creations with unusual/uniform extensions right after shadow deletion means encryption is underway - isolate the host IMMEDIATELY.

Node.Condition: Shadow-copy deletion by a non-backup process/account, especially with mass file changes following.
Node.Result: True Positive (Ransomware - ISOLATE HOST NOW, activate ransomware IR)

Node.Condition: A documented backup admin rotating shadow storage/catalogs under a maintenance window.
Recovery-inhibition command with unclear context and no encryption signs yet.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-RECOVERY-CMD, INV-02-RECOVERY-ENCRYPT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the maintenance; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A ransomware precursor (recovery inhibition before encryption).

Indicators.Item: Shadow deletion by a non-backup context.

SOCAction.Item: ISOLATE the host immediately; activate ransomware IR.
Identify patient zero and scope; protect backups; hunt the same command on other hosts.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
